symptoms: Site can remain visually trapped on the boot loader even though HTML is delivered.
Bottom magic dock can look vertically crooked on iPhone safe-area devices.
confirmed_causes: PWA remained a static import in the critical app module, so any PWA-layer failure could abort the entire app before boot completion.
The legacy index bootstrap still registers sw.js?v=208 on window load, competing with later worker generations.

The dock already offsets itself above env(safe-area-inset-bottom), while a later runtime rule also applied the safe-area as internal padding-bottom, compressing the five dock items inside a fixed 75/78px height.
fixes: Remove PWA from the app's static-import critical path and dynamically load it only after the visual shell has opened.
Release the boot loader immediately after critical V180 CSS is verified; navigation runs afterward with a timeout and cannot keep the site closed.
Emergency fail-open also removes the loader if critical CSS validation itself fails.
PWA auto-start remains only on dedicated install pages; app pages start it explicitly after boot.
Register the V326 Service Worker repeatedly after load so it wins over the legacy V208 inline registration.
Service Worker installation no longer fails because an optional cache asset is temporarily unavailable.
Static script/style fetches use cache reload before falling back to cached copies.
New dock-stability-v326.css removes duplicated safe-area padding and locks the 5-column geometry without redesigning the approved dock.
preserve: Approved Home Orb visual and gesture engine
Five-item dock identity and central mini Orb
